searchText: It's been a little while since I've posted in here, so I thought I'd post an update. I'm still running validators for all 20 client pairs using the develpment branches for each client on Goerli, and they're all functioning well at the moment. Links to the validator dashboard and individual links for each client pair: https://seamonkey.tech/goerli/goerli_validators.html Tmuxinator config that loads everything: https://seamonkey.tech/goerli/goerli.yml Some disk usage stats: ``` 643G nimbus-erigon 639G lighthouse-erigon 431G lodestar-erigon 390G teku-erigon 344G lighthouse-nethermind 330G prysm-nethermind 329G prysm-erigon 318G nimbus-nethermind 312G teku-nethermind 304G lighthouse-geth 288G lodestar-nethermind 281G nimbus-geth 273G lodestar-besu 270G teku-geth 268G lighthouse-besu 248G lodestar-geth 241G nimbus-besu 239G teku-besu 218G prysm-geth 142G prysm-besu ``` Is this besu with checkpoint sync (that doesn't backfill iirc)? And Prysm was lacking something like that as well Don't quite understand how geth can be so low though, also not backfilling? I was curious how much space our nodes use, and here are some numbers for the mainnet nodes: (note that Besu has been resynced from scratch with their bonsai structure, thats why its so appealing``` 1.6T erigon-lodestar 1.6T erigon-prysm 1.5T erigon-nimbus 1.5T erigon-lighthouse 1.4T erigon-teku 1.2T nethermind-lodestar 1.1T nethermind-nimbus 1.1T nethermind-lighthouse 1.1T nethermind-prysm 1.0T nethermind-teku 1.0T geth-lodestar 947G geth-lighthouse 946G geth-prysm 923G geth-nimbus 886G geth-teku 688G besu-lodestar 645G besu-prysm 604G besu-nimbus 631G besu-lighthouse 577G besu-teku ``` (I think a freshly synced nethermind should also take up ~700G now?) Yes, besu is using `--sync-mode=X_CHECKPOINT`. All non-default configuration parameters that can be defined on the command line are in the goerli.yml linked above. prysm-besu was most recently re-synced after some invalid forkchoice issues which have since been resolved. The next version of Teku will also support `--data-storage-mode=MINIMAL` which only keeps historic blocks as far back as required by the spec (~5 months) rather than all the way to genesis (and like `PRUNE` doesn't store finalized states). It won't be the default but will get the consensus layer disk usage to be almost fixed size (around 42Gb on MainNet). I believe Nimbus is looking at supporting block pruning too. would this mean that theoretically eventually (if everyone starts using pruning), then nobody going to be able to sync from genesis? but only with checkpoint sync? Potentially yes. Though no one should be syncing from genesis either. That said we do need to build out ways to get these historic blocks to support creating archive nodes and for historic records etc. The Nimbus team have done a bunch of work on that. We've been holding off supporting block pruning since before genesis so that we'd get those systems setup, but it's a bit of a chicken and egg problem. Supporting block pruning but not making it default is basically cracking the egg to try and get the chicken moving.... Might have strained that analogy a bit too much...
